teaser: Gameweek 4 hands out the fixtures very unevenly. Four teams get a 2/5 rating and a home crowd, while the Manchester derby throws two 4/5s at each other and drags a lot of expensive assets down with it. There are also two sub-2% owned defenders in real form walking into kind fixtures, which is the sort of thing that wins you a mini-league week.
fullWriteup:
Start with the green. Liverpool (2/5, home) host a Fulham side rated 4/5 for the trip. Chelsea (2/5, home) get Hull, who are on a 4/5. Crystal Palace (2/5, home) take on Ipswich and Leeds (2/5, home) welcome Newcastle. Coventry vs Brighton is the rare one where both sides are marked kind at 2/5, so nobody in that game is being punished by the ratings.

The red side is more concentrated. Manchester United vs Manchester City is 4/5 for both, which is bad news for the two highest-form premium assets in the game right now: Bruno Fernandes (form 9.0, £12.0m, 44.2% owned) and Erling Haaland (form 8.0, £15.5m, 71.2% owned). You're not selling either on one fixture, but if you were thinking about captaincy, there are better-rated homes for the armband. Same logic applies to Cherki (8.3) and Gvardiol (7.3) in that match, and to Mbeumo (7.0). Nottingham Forest at Villa Park (4/5) and Fulham at Anfield (4/5) are the other two to avoid.

The cleanest form-plus-fixture overlap is at Chelsea and Liverpool. Cole Palmer (form 7.0, £9.7m, 25.2%) and João Pedro (form 7.0, £7.7m, 73.1%) both get a 2/5 home fixture, and Palmer at a quarter ownership is arguably still the better route in. Alexander Isak (form 7.7, £9.1m, 22.3%) is the pick of the forwards this week on the numbers: second-best form of any striker in the top 25 and Liverpool's 2/5 home rating against a Fulham side marked 4/5. At 22.3% owned he's not even a crowd move yet.

Arsenal's trip to Sunderland is only rated 3/5 for them against a 4/5 for the hosts, so the in-form Gunners are playable rather than avoidable. Ødegaard (form 8.0, £6.7m) at 16.5% owned is the interesting one there, cheaper and less owned than Saka (7.3, £9.5m, 11.5%) is expensive. Calafiori (7.3) is already at 48.6% owned, so he's the hold rather than the move.

For differentials, two defenders stand out and both are effectively unowned. Ben Chilwell (form 7.0, £4.5m, 0.4% owned) has Palace at home on a 2/5. Jayden Bogle (form 7.3, £4.5m, 1.8% owned) has Leeds at home on a 2/5. Same price, same fixture rating, and between them they're owned by fewer managers than most bench fodder. Maitland-Niles (form 7.0, £4.5m, 0.2%) is a third option but Everton's Spurs trip is only an average 3/5, so he's a tier below.

Further up, Alex Scott (form 8.0, £6.1m, 5.3% owned) is the standout cheap midfielder on form alone, though Bournemouth's home fixture against Brentford is a flat 3/5 for both sides, so it's a form punt rather than a fixture punt. Tavernier (7.0, £6.0m, 3.5%) is the same bet at a slightly lower price. And one warning: Hull have five players in the top 25 for form, including Tzolakis (8.7) and Ajayi (8.3), but they're on a 4/5 at Stamford Bridge. Let that one pass and revisit next week.
